response.content:
Based on available information, the following company with an AI focus hired a Country Manager for Denmark in 2026:

- **impact.com** — Named **Nikolai Lundstrøm Brink** as Country Manager for Denmark. impact.com is a partnership management platform that leverages AI-powered optimization. Nikolai, previously Head of Sales at Adtraction Denmark, was appointed to grow impact.com's presence in the Danish market from the company's base in Aarhus.

Other companies that appointed Country Managers for Denmark in 2026 (though not primarily AI companies) include:

- **Avanza** (Swedish fintech/neobank) — Appointed **Christian Sillesen** as Country Manager for Denmark in September 2026, joining from Lunar, to lead the company's organic expansion into the Danish savings market.

No additional AI-focused companies with a specific "Country Manager for Denmark" appointment in 2026 were identified in the available sources. If you're looking for a broader set of AI-related executive hires in Denmark, the search could be refined further.

 Avanza Bank AB - Investor News 

# Christian Sillesen appointed Country Manager for Avanza in Denmark [...] Christian Sillesen has been appointed Country Manager for Avanza in Denmark. He joins Avanza from the Danish neobank Lunar, where he served as Head of Commercial for Retail & Business Banking. Christian will assume his position on October 12 and will lead efforts to build Avanza's presence and offering in the Danish market.

In April, Avanza announced its intention to establish operations in Denmark. The expansion will be organic, with launch scheduled for H2 2027. [...] "It is with great anticipation that we welcome Christian to Avanza and the role of Country Manager in Denmark. We have been looking for a business-driven leader with a deep understanding of the consumer market and a proven ability to build a business from the ground up. Christian has all of this, and in combination with his entrepreneurial personality, it makes him the right person to lead our expansion and challenge the Danish savings market," says Gustaf Unger, CEO of Avanza.
